[ContextualTasks] Use browser theme in Guest mode

`ShouldUseDarkModeForProfile` previously checked `IsOffTheRecord()`,
which returned true for both Incognito and Guest sessions even though
`ThemeService` only forces dark mode for Incognito profiles. Restricting
the forced dark mode check to `IsIncognitoProfile()` allows Guest
sessions to follow the browser color scheme from `ThemeService`.

[WebUI Toolbar] Shrink Avatar button text when there's no space.

Previously, the WebUI toolbar's avatar button was all-or-nothing: if its
label didn't fit, the whole button overflowed. This CL shrinks it the
way the Views avatar button does when kToolbarProfileChipResizing is
enabled. Since that feature is now enabled by default, the WebUI toolbar
always behaves as if it's enabled.

As the available space decreases, the avatar button shrinks through a
number of phases, down to only having the button visible.

OverflowableButtonMixin::shouldPreventOverflow() is now public, and the
mixin's updated() now only un-hides the button when overflow is
prevented, rather than calling setToPreferredWidth(), which subclasses
may override. A layout is requested in either case.

Known limitation: When the label text first appears (or is removed) and
the toolbar has to hide other controls to make room, the label's
animation is skipped. The layout pass sets all controls to min width,
which cancels the CSS animation, before attempting to expanding it up to
its preferred width, so the label will appear all at once, rather than
animating the text into view. This isn't a regression, but is a polish
issue we may want to work on down the line. Fixing it properly likely
requires JS-driven animation, rather than relying solely on CSS. This
would also remove our dependency on ResizeObserver, which causes
width-respecting layout to happen only after animation-induced visual
refreshes, which can cause the toolbar to exceed its maximum size for a
frame.

[🌷] Deflake ClipboardImageFileProviderTest#testClipboardSetImage

ClipboardImageFileProviderTest#testClipboardSetImage flaked with
FileNotFoundException because ShareImageFileUtils.clearSharedImages()
scheduled on AsyncTask.SERIAL_EXECUTOR during deferred startup could
execute after saveImage() created the temporary image file on disk
but before ClipboardImpl.setImageUri() published the new clip
metadata on the UI thread. Drain AsyncTask.SERIAL_EXECUTOR at the end
of setUp() after activity launch and run Clipboard mutations on the
UI thread.

mac: Reduce flickering when toggling bookmark bar in mac fullscreen

There is a flicker at the bottom of content area when toggling bookmark
bar in mac fullscreen, with "Always Show Toolbar in Full Screen"
enabled.

The root cause is in BrowserViewTabbedLayoutImpl::OnLayoutParamsChanged.
The calculation of visual client area is wrong there.

infra/config: Demote ios-simulator long-pole unittests to ci_only

Mark components_unittests and ios_chrome_unittests as ci_only = True on
ci/ios-simulator (and mirrored try builders try/ios-simulator and
try/ios-simulator-exp).

Both suites are currently the long-pole targets for ios-simulator and
cannot be sharded because of how the iOS test runner handles test
filtering on retries after crashes. Demoting them to CI-only avoids
blocking CQ while sharding support is investigated.

[Omnibox] Add pull-to-refresh tests for Omnibox minimization

Behind ClankOmniboxMinimization (arm = "hide_on_same_origin_nav",
suppress_pull_to_refresh_reveal = true), keeping the Omnibox hidden
across same-origin navigations requires a two-step pull-to-refresh at
the top of the page: the first downward pull reveals the Omnibox
without reloading, and a second pull once the Omnibox is fully visible
triggers reload.

Add unit and integration tests ahead of crbug.com/579544393:
- Wire SwipeRefreshHandlerUnitTest against real tab and browser-controls
  components instead of Mockito mocks. Add two-step suppression tests,
  including positive minHeight (disabled with crbug.com/579544393), and
  enabled guardrails for flag/param off, minimize_omnibox arm,
  non-tabbed browsers, bottom controls, force-hidden controls, Auto,
  TV, and XR.
- Add an end-to-end Public Transit test in BrowserControlsPTTest
  (disabled with crbug.com/579544393) verifying two-step pull-to-refresh
  after a same-origin navigation keeps top controls scrolled off.

[IA][BottomBar] Add a long-press menu

Long-pressing the top toolbar opens a menu, but long-pressing empty
space on the bottom bar did nothing. The bottom bar now shows a similar
menu with "Customize appearance", which opens the Appearance settings
where the bottom bar can be turned off.

It uses the same standard long-press as the top toolbar, set on the
whole bar, so the buttons keep their own long-press and only empty space
opens the menu. This makes the bar long-clickable, like the top toolbar.
It still consumes all touches so they don't fall through to the page.

The menu only shows when the Toolbar switch is offered in Settings,
since that's where it takes the user.

The long_press_menu_enabled param is a kill switch. With it off, the
bar never gets the long-press listener and keeps its old touch
handling.

[mac][viz] Support non-uniform rounded corners on CA backdrop filters

Support CSS backdrop-filter overlay promotion on elements with
elliptical ovals or asymmetric multi-radius rounded corners that cannot
be represented natively via CALayer cornerRadius + maskedCorners:

- Build a scaled cubic Bezier CGPath in CreatePathForRRect() and fall
  back to a CAShapeLayer mask on CABackdropLayer in
  CARendererLayerTree::ContentLayer when ApplyCornerRadiusToCALayer()
  returns false, clearing the mask if bounds return to uniform corners.
- Lift the IsMaskableRRect() restriction in ExtractBackdropFilter() and
  the matching bounds check in CARendererLayerTree::ScheduleCALayer().
- Add unit tests in accelerated_widget_mac_unittests and viz_unittests.

Manual test pages:
https://benoitlben.github.io/test-pages/backdrop-tests/index.html

build: Switch GCC builds to -std=c11 and -std=c++20/-std=c++23

Align GCC compiler flags with Clang by passing -std=c11 and
-std=c++20/-std=c++23 instead of -std=gnu*, and define _GNU_SOURCE
unconditionally on Linux, ChromeOS, Android, and AIX. Defining
_GNU_SOURCE explicitly also fixes C compilation on GCC (such as
third_party/libdrm), since -std=gnu11 did not define _GNU_SOURCE.

In standards-conforming mode, GCC only retains the comma before
##__VA_ARGS__ when the variadic parameter is the sole macro parameter.
Replace ##__VA_ARGS__ with C++20 __VA_OPT__ in ARG_COUNT() in
components/services/app_service/public/cpp/macros.h, which is the only
first-party macro in chromium/src with an unnamed-only variadic
parameter list, and add compile-time assertions covering zero and
non-zero arguments.

[Dictation] Gate page context extraction on Optimization Guide hint

Only extract page context for Dictation when the Optimization Guide has
a DICTATION_ELIGIBLE hint for the page whose DictationMetadata marks it
eligible, otherwise send empty context.

The server attaches the hint to any page it has a safety verdict for
(page- and sitechunk-level porn and child-safety signals), with the
verdict in the metadata. The check uses cached hints so starting a
stream is never delayed.

[🌷] Deflake MessageCardProviderTest#testDismissPriceMessage

In BlankUiTestActivity on Android 15+, the un-inset root FrameLayout
places the first RecyclerView item under the top system status and
desktop caption bars, causing raw Espresso clicks on the top-right
close button to be intercepted by the system bar window. Set
fitsSystemWindows(true) on the test container, use Public Transit's
waitForView().click() for the card buttons, and re-enable
testDismissPriceMessage on desktop.

[Glic] Populate error and timing diagnostics in TaskUpdate metadata

Remote ExperimentalTriggering callers require live per-session failure
attribution and phase diagnostics on terminal TaskUpdate responses to
distinguish Chrome-side pre-client/load failures from web-client errors
and handle retryability. Asynchronous client-side UMA/Structured Metrics
cannot return these signals on the wire or join them per session.

Populate diagnostic fields in TaskUpdate.metadata while keeping existing
TaskUpdate.data payloads unchanged:
- Subscribe to GlicInvokeOptions::SetOnErrorWithDiagnostics() via
  InvokeErrorDiagnosticsPasskey, map Chrome-originated invocation
  (including external supersede), Mojo disconnect, mid-flight teardown,
  missing browser window, and disallowed web-actuation policy failures
  to bounded chrome_error_code values, and forward non-empty invocation
  diagnostics opaquely as chrome_invoke_diagnostics.
- Omit chrome_error_code on unlisted invocation errors and web-client
  terminal updates so web-client error codes in TaskUpdate.data remain
  authoritative.
- Latch elapsed durations from task_start_time_ to panel open, client
  connection, first response, and terminal state (resetting task-scoped
  milestones on non-continuation re-triggers), and attach milestone
  flags and phase timings on terminal actuation updates.

Design doc:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qqcCOq-g4rSIIUGRguIY9Tu8VpBVEazxBt2T8QsBpGc/edit

[User Ed] Add IPH group for Clank NTP theme promos

This change defines the kClankNewTabPageThemeCustomizationPromosGroup
Feature Engagement group and enrolls both Clank New Tab Page theme
customization promo features into it. Without a shared group
configuration, the 3-dot menu NTP theme customization IPH and the NTP
theme customization promo Magic Stack card have no shared cooldown in
the Feature Engagement Tracker. It declares the group feature flag,
registers it in the group list, defines its 7-day trigger cooldown in
the group configuration, and adds the group to both NTP theme promo
feature configurations.

[ContextualTasks] Fix dark mode toolbar icon color

`ChromeContentBrowserClient` previously only overrode the renderer
`preferred_color_scheme` for `chrome://contextual-tasks` when an
explicit `cs` query parameter was present on the outer WebUI URL, while
`app.css` relied on the `cr_shared_vars.css` media query fallback for
`--toolbar-button-icon-color`. When the side panel opened in dark mode
without an outer `cs` parameter (such as Lens region searches in an
off-the-record window while the browser color mode remained light), the
toolbar buttons rendered in dark gray against the dark toolbar
background.

Resolving `preferred_color_scheme` via `ShouldUseDarkMode` and
explicitly setting `--toolbar-button-icon-color` in the dark mode
stylesheets keeps toolbar button icons legible whenever Contextual Tasks
renders in dark mode.

[Glic][Android] Mount native FRE overlay in GlicBottomSheetContent

Mount GlicBottomSheetFreCoordinator over the expanded content group in
GlicBottomSheetContent while native FRE is active, and wire the Java
component provider and Custom Tab launcher:

- Provide SettingsCustomTabLauncher to glic via GlicNavigationUtils
  from TabbedRootUiCoordinator (glic cannot depend on chrome_java).
  Both Glic launchers are now set whenever the Glic flags are on and
  before initializeTabBottomSheetManagers(), because creating the
  manager can synchronously call OnManagerInitialized() -> Show() ->
  createContent(), which mounts the card.
- Track the active GlicBottomSheetContent in
  GlicBottomSheetComponentProvider so configureNativeFre(boolean) mounts
  or tears down the native FRE overlay across sheet recreations.
- Derive enterprise status from GlicEnabling.isEnterpriseAccount, route
  the FRE close button to onBackPressed, tear down the overlay on
  accept before notifying native, and expose the FRE ScrollView
  vertical scroll offset to the sheet swipe detector.

[TTC][CAL][1/N] Register target tab on ActorTask in OpenKnownPageTool and crashed-tab reload

Why this is needed for CAL:
Critical Action Logging (CAL) records agent navigations in Chrome
History only when the navigating tab is registered as an active surface
on the session ActorTask. Without registering the tab before
OpenKnownPageTool or a crashed-tab reload navigates, those navigations
are not attributed to the agent.

What this change does:
OpenKnownPageTool constructs NavigateTool directly instead of going
through ActorTask::Act early tab registration. Register the target
surface in OpenKnownPageTool::UpdateTaskBeforeInvoke so HistoryService
attributes the navigation to the acting ActorTask. In
ToolController::ReloadPage, register the active tab on the session
ActorTask before reloading a crashed tab directly.

Revert "[DW] Keep caption bar transparent until uncustomized bar is present"

This reverts commit 412c7e197e70a88fa8416f861c954d9e1852bf52.

Reason for revert: Keeping the caption bar transparent when caption
bounding rects are empty causes the OS to dispatch transient caption
bar insets during a fullscreen back gesture, exiting fullscreen
mid-swipe and navigating the tab back (crbug.com/583470708).

Failure Link: N/A

Original change's description:
> [DW] Keep caption bar transparent until uncustomized bar is present
>
> On some Android 16 tablet devices, the OS ignores task appearance
> updates during the drag-to-desktop transition animation and inflates
> the caption view asynchronously, leaving an opaque caption bar over
> the tab strip until focus changes.
>
> - Evaluate caption bar transparency on every caption bar insets update
>   rather than only when desktop windowing mode changes.
> - Keep the caption bar background transparent while Chrome customizes
>   the app header or when no caption bar bounding rects are present
>   (e.g. in fullscreen, or while transitioning into desktop windowing
>   mode).
> - Clear the transparent appearance only when a caption bar with
>   bounding rects is present and Chrome does not customize it.
>

[🌷] Deflake VoiceToolbarButtonControllerTest NTP and dialog tests

VoiceToolbarButtonControllerTest flaked in batched runs due to
asynchronous modal dialog button updates, cleared toolbar state across
batched tests, and missing first-run experience suppression.
Additionally, the previous deflake CL was reverted because navigating
to the NTP via getOriginalNativeNtpUrl() failed deterministically on
Desktop Android where the WebUI NTP override expects
getOriginalNtpUrl(). This change dynamically resolves the appropriate
NTP URL based on whether WebUI NTP override is enabled, polls on the
UI thread for the button to become disabled during modal dialogs, sets
the adaptive toolbar state in @Before for each test (as
AdaptiveToolbarStatePredictor#setToolbarStateForTesting resets
automatically via ResettersForTesting), restores the programmatic page
reload to trigger the real navigation update pipeline when voice search
is toggled, and suppresses first-run prompts.

parent
8e3fd1e949738333909fc54a372f8b328ef41be6 [ diff ] 
[Wayland] Use the xdg-role ancestor as the activation token surface

Clicking another profile in the profile menu didn't raise that
profile's window on GNOME Wayland; GNOME showed a "<title> is ready"
notification instead.

The profile menu is a WaylandBubble, i.e. a wl_subsurface of the browser
window. The click closes the bubble, and the xdg_activation_v1 token for
the other window is then requested with the bubble's surface as the
requestor (the pointer-focused window). Compositors compare the token's
surface with their keyboard- or pointer-focused toplevel/popup surface
(mutter: token_can_activate()), so a subsurface, which here is already
detached, never matches and the activation is refused.

Map windows without an xdg role to the closest ancestor that has one
(WaylandWindow::GetXdgParentWindow()) when choosing the requestor
surface.

[iOS] Forward suspicious site warnings through SafeBrowsingClient

Plumb non-blocking suspicious site verdicts from UrlCheckerDelegateImpl
to SafeBrowsingClient on iOS:
- Add SafeBrowsingClient::OnSuspiciousSiteWarningTriggered() across iOS
  Safe Browsing clients (with no-op stubs in WebView and Chrome until
  SuspiciousSiteTabHelper lands).
- Implement UrlCheckerDelegateImpl::ShowSuspiciousSiteWarning() gated on
  Enhanced Protection, kSuspiciousSiteWarnings, non-OTR state, and
  client block-eligibility checks (suppressing prerendered pages).

Design doc: go/suss-sites-ios-dd

[GEiC] Restyle the relaunch prompt to match the mocks

The provider-change relaunch prompt reused the plain Glic error panel
styling. Restyle it to match the UX mocks for light and dark mode: a
bordered card with a larger headline, a blue pill button, and a soft
blue glow behind the card. Both the webview and NoWebview panels pick
this up because they share glic.css.

Use custom cursor size in CursorLoader instead of large cursor

CursorLoader only needs a target cursor size, not the large cursor
concept. Replace SetSize() and SetLargeCursorSizeInDip() with
SetCustomCursorSize(std::optional<int>), and let
NativeCursorManagerAsh map the large cursor state to it.

This is the first step to generalize the internal cursor size
mechanism. The large cursor concept stays in the UI and
accessibility code.

This is 1st CL to eliminate LargeCursor concept from framework, but
it will stay as Settings/Accessibility concept.

CONV=a3352fe4-469b-4b6a-8dec-e7d5a77640bf

[mac][viz] Support saturate, brightness, and contrast in CA backdrop filters

Extend CoreAnimation CSS backdrop-filter overlay promotion to support
color-matrix filter operations alongside or independently of Gaussian
blur:

- Probe CAFilter colorMatrix (inputColorMatrix) and expose
  CreateCAColorMatrixFilter() in ca_backdrop_filter_api.mm behind
  BUILDFLAG(IS_MAC).
- Add an optional 4x5 color_matrix field on ui::CABackdropFilterParams
  and attach both gaussianBlur and colorMatrix CAFilters when present in
  CARendererLayerTree::ContentLayer.
- Compose saturate(), brightness(), and contrast() operations via
  SkColorMatrix in ExtractBackdropFilter(), skipping identity operations.
- Add unit tests in accelerated_widget_mac_unittests and viz_unittests.

Manual test pages:
https://benoitlben.github.io/test-pages/backdrop-tests/index.html

[User Ed] Add IPH feature for NTP theme promo Magic Stack card

This change defines the kIPHNewTabPageThemeCustomizationMagicStackFeature
feature flag and its FeatureConfig so that the New Tab Page theme
customization Magic Stack card can be tracked by the Feature Engagement
Tracker. Without a Feature Engagement entry, the Magic Stack card
cannot share a cooldown group with the 3-dot menu NTP theme
customization IPH. It adds the feature constant declarations in C++ and
Java, registers the feature in the Feature Engagement feature list and
default configuration, and adds the corresponding histogram and user
action entries.

[RA] Accept a full origin as the remote actor credential sharing domain

Start() always prepended "https://", which broke senders that pass a
full origin (iOS Gemini sends "https://example.com"; desktop sends a
bare host). Only prepend the scheme when absent, honor the sender's
scheme otherwise, and reject input that does not form a valid origin.

QueryPasswordStores() now derives its digest from `origin_` instead of
re-building the URL from the raw string.

2e0f025ad50428170c4f9f8c080e0ce2eb6a1e57 [ diff ] 
[Android] Avoid redundant byte[] copies when saving PersistedTabData

Protobuf PersistedTabData serializers previously returned read-only
ByteBuffers via toByteString().asReadOnlyByteBuffer(), forcing
LevelDBPersistedTabDataStorage.toByteArray() to allocate and copy a
second byte[] on every save. Return
ByteBuffer.wrap(build().toByteArray()) instead so toByteArray() reuses
the backing heap array directly without an intermediate copy, and
std::move the native std::string payload into
PersistedStateContentProto.

Also tighten the toByteArray() fast-path check to require position() ==
0 and limit() == array().length, and read [position(), limit()) via
duplicate() on fallback so sub-range and sliced buffers copy only their
active slice.

[Paint Preview] Set initiator origin for link clicks

Navigating to a link clicked in a Paint Preview previously used default
LoadUrlParams without an initiator origin or HTTP(S) scheme check.
Restrict Paint Preview link navigations to HTTP(S) URLs and mark them as
renderer-initiated with an opaque initiator origin to match other
captured and restored navigation flows.

[Base] Re-disable `AnyCriticalThreadHung` on iOS

https://crrev.com/c/8636570 re-enabled
`HangWatcherAnyCriticalThreadTests.AnyCriticalThreadHung` on iOS after
fixing a dangling pointer in `HangWatcherTest.BestEffortHistograms`.
The test is still flaky on almost every gardened iOS configuration (an
actual issue observed on LUCI), so this CL disables it again on iOS
only.

The `ScopedClosureRunner` that resets the shared last-foreground-time
pointer, which https://crrev.com/c/8636570 also added, is kept. It fixes
a real dangling pointer, and Android was already flaky before it landed
(see below), so the fix did not cause the Android flakiness.

Rule used (this CL keeps a test running unless one of these matches on
gardened builders): R1 >=90% failed or errored; R2 >=2 failed verdicts
(excluding builds with >5 other failing tests and failure bursts) and
>=1%; R3 >=30 verdicts and >=10% flaky. A flaky verdict failed and then
passed on retry, so the build stayed green.

iOS, R3 (flaky/total verdicts, 0 failed verdicts):
- ios-simulator-noncq: iOS18 iPhone 3,728/4,016 (92.8%), iOS26 iPad
  3,632/4,016 (90.4%), iOS27 iPad 1,752/2,008 (87.3%), iOS27 iPhone
  3,328/4,016 (82.9%), iOS18 iPad 3,232/4,016 (80.5%), iOS26 iPhone
  2,800/4,016 (69.7%).
- ios-device: iOS18 iPhone 8,384/11,088 (75.6%).
- ios-simulator: iOS18 iPad 1,928/2,632 (73.3%), iOS27 iPad
  1,408/2,632 (53.5%), iOS27 iPhone 1,320/2,632 (50.2%), iOS26 iPhone
  1,224/2,632 (46.5%), iOS18 iPhone 632/2,632 (24.0%).
- ios-simulator-full-configs: 36.3%-63.0% on all 6 configurations.
Only `ios-asan` (iOS26 iPad 88/1,472 = 6.0%, iOS26 iPhone 80/1,472 =
5.4%) is below the threshold. Since 18 of the 20 gardened iOS
configurations match, the test is disabled on all of iOS.

Other platforms keep running the test:
- Linux, Mac, Windows, ChromeOS and Fuchsia gardened builders: 0 flaky
  and 0 failed verdicts.
- Android gardened builders are 35.1%-47.9% flaky after the landing, but
  they were already 37.5%-49.6% flaky in the 7 days before it, so
  https://crrev.com/c/8636570 did not cause it. This CL doesn't change
  Android.

Data: windows from the landing of https://crrev.com/c/8636570
(2026-11-02T16:00:48Z) to 2026-11-09T12:00:00Z, and the 7 days before
the landing for the comparison, `chromium` project, summed over the 8
parameterized test IDs:

    v=~/.agents/skills/revert-fix-all-test/scripts/verdicts.py
    t=AnyCriticalThreadHung
    python3 $v 2026-11-02T16:00:48Z 2026-11-09T12:00:00Z $t \
      --chromium --builder
    python3 $v 2026-10-26T16:00:48Z 2026-11-02T16:00:48Z $t \
      --chromium --builder

Test history (one of the 8 test IDs):
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/%3A%2F%2Fbase%5C%3Abase_unittests%21gtest%3A%3AHangWatcherAnyCriticalThreadTests%23AnyCriticalThreadHung%2FCriticalProcessAndThreadSpotChecks.MainThreadIsCritical

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

[Extensions] Disallow nullable WebIDL dictionary members for now

Nullable types (?) on WebIDL dictionary members are not currently
processed by web_idl_schema.py, and existing usages in
developer_private.webidl and document_scan.webidl were accidental
holdovers from the legacy IDL optional syntax (in WebIDL, dictionary
members are already optional unless marked `required`).

Remove the erroneous `?` suffixes from those schema files and raise a
SchemaCompilerError if a dictionary member type is marked nullable,
with a TODO to support nullable dictionary members in the future.

[WebOTP] Ignore Abort() with no pending request

WebOTPService::Abort() reported a bad message, killing the renderer,
when no request was pending. But a well-behaved renderer can send such
an Abort(), because the browser may finish a request before the renderer
gets the response. For example, if a page aborts two requests that share
an AbortSignal, the second request has already cancelled the first, so
one Abort() finds nothing pending.

Ignore such calls, as there is nothing to abort. FedCM does the same:
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:content/browser/webid/request_handler.cc;l=219-224;drc=57b8d0a25c7651a77782edb8f12c2efb13c28de6

Fixed: 580787570
Test: content_unittests --gtest_filter=WebOTPServiceTest.*

[glic] Implement UpdateGlicSplitButtonUi in desktop Views containers

Implements GlicSplitButtonDelegate::UpdateGlicSplitButtonUi on both
TabStripActionContainer and ToolbarView via shared helpers on
GlicActorTaskIcon.

When secondary activities exist (such as active background tasks or
ready conversation responses), the secondary button updates its icon
(chevron or spark) and nudge label according to GlicSplitButtonUiState,
and activating it toggles the GlicActivityListBubble via
GlicSplitButtonController.

Stack context: Wires up desktop Views to GlicSplitButtonUiState from the
previous CL; legacy GlicActor* names are renamed in the top CL.

[fuchsia] Re-enable MDnsTest refresh query tests in net_unittests

MDnsTest.RefreshQuery was previously disabled on Fuchsia because the
test ran with real wall-clock timers and flaked under load, and
MDnsTest.RefreshQueryMaxTTL copied the same Fuchsia exclusion when it
was added. Since MDnsTest now uses a mock time source and clamped
int64_t timer conversions, re-enable both refresh query tests on
Fuchsia.

[viz] Promote CSS backdrop-filter blur() RPDQs to macOS CALayer overlays

Promote eligible AggregatedRenderPassDrawQuads with CSS backdrop-filter
Gaussian blur to macOS CoreAnimation overlays when
kCoreAnimationBackdropFilter is enabled:

- Plumb CABackdropFilterParams from FromRenderPassQuad() through
  OverlayCandidate and OutputPresenterGL to CARendererLayerParams.
- Scale single-blur radius into RenderPass local space via filters_scale
  (with quad_to_target_transform applied by CARendererLayerTree).
- Validate and clip backdrop_filter_bounds for hardware-maskable RRects
  via IsMaskableRRect(), rejecting RPDQs with unsupported filter chains,
  non-uniform corner radii, foreground filters, masks, or non-unit
  opacity so SkiaRenderer handles them.
- Clear rpdq_params.backdrop_filter in
  SkiaRenderer::PrepareRenderPassOverlay to skip redundant GPU passes.
- Add 15 unit tests in viz_unittests.

Color-matrix adjustments (saturate, brightness, contrast) and
non-uniform rounded corner masks are added in follow-up CLs.

Manual test pages:
https://benoitlben.github.io/test-pages/backdrop-tests/index.html

[TabUI Virtualization] Apply group membership updates from the provider

When a tab joins or leaves a group, the data provider tells
TabListMediator, but the mediator dropped the update. In provider mode
the group card kept its old tab count, and a closed tab that wasn't the
last in its group stayed observed, since no other provider event
detaches it.

The mediator now refreshes the group card and stops observing tabs that
left the group. In the vertical tab strip, a tab row that moves into or
out of an expanded group keeps its own card, so that card's group color
and id are updated too. Selection and pin state updates are still
ignored and will be handled separately.

Free PolicyData::policy_value after policy install

This saves up to 2MB of RAM + 2MB per profile, with no downsides.

CloudPolicyStore retains the serialized policy payload in heap memory
for the lifetime of the store. Large policy configurations, such as
ExtensionSettings, keep megabytes of redundant bytes allocated in
PolicyData::policy_value after decoding into PolicyMap.

Calculate and cache policy_value_hash_ during SetPolicy(), then free the
payload string buffer. Update PolicyInvalidator to read the cached hash
instead of accessing the cleared payload string.

[🌷] Deflake SensitiveContentTest#testSensitiveContentClientObserver

testSensitiveContentClientObserver intermittently flaked due to a
race between asynchronous autofill DOM form sensitivity updates on
the UI thread and immediate synchronous assertions on the test
thread. To fix this, encapsulate UI-thread polling via CriteriaHelper
directly on the test observer and safely manage its registration
lifecycle within a try-finally block to avoid batch test
contamination.

[fuchsia] Remove build_version.txt dependency in component_storage_test

Fuchsia's core/feedback component is removing legacy build.version and
/data/build_version.txt support (https://fxrev.dev/1961945), which
breaks component_storage_test when pulling build_version.txt from
core/feedback's /data storage.

Instead of relying on internal core/feedback files, push, list, pull,
and delete a temporary file created by the test itself across both data
and tmp storage capabilities so component storage coverage no longer
couples to Fuchsia component internals.

Add RedirectionSessionHost to own IMMRSession for MMR

RedirectionSessionHost is a per source host that owns an MMR session,
MediaRemoter, and RedirectionRpcDispatcher. It connects the MediaRemoter
to the browser's mojo pipes and creates RedirectionRemotingSenders for
audio and video streams. When RPC_ACQUIRE_DEMUXER receives the demuxer
handles, it creates the MMR streams and attaches them to the senders.

MediaRemoter::Stop handles setting state_ to REMOTING_DISABLED for RPC
errors or data stream errors to avoid setting state_ after calling Stop.
Stop calls RestartMirroringStreaming. Both RedirectionSessionHost and
OpenscreenSessionHost can destroy MediaRemoter in
RestartMirroringStreaming, which would result in a use after free if
state_ is then changed after Stop returns.

3f2f8b645e0d98d0322a51fe22c32bd116645aa3
parent
90528e92585ab9c2a582eb03243cbf8a02a2e130 [ diff ] 
[extensions] Avoid cloning args in ExtensionFunction::GetMutableArgs

https://crrev.com/c/6652358 stopped unconditionally cloning arguments on
`ExtensionFunction` dispatch, instead lazily cloning `args_` into
`original_args_` when `GetMutableArgs()` is called to support
`GetOriginalArgs()`. While most APIs never call `GetMutableArgs()`,
`chrome.storage` always does [1], so large `chrome.storage.<area>.set()`
payloads are still cloned and later destroyed on the UI thread in
`StorageFrontend::OnWriteFinished` (`0.19%` of browser main-thread
congestion on Windows Stable [2] and `0.18%` on macOS Stable [3]).

The pprof filter selects `GetMutableArgs()` and `base::Value::~Value()`
under `StorageFrontend::OnWriteFinished` -> `~ExtensionFunction()` [4].
Since `chrome.storage.<area>.set()` moves `args_` to the backend
sequence [5], its `args_` is empty by `OnWriteFinished` and `~Value()`
there destroys the cloned `original_args_`.

This CL skips cloning `args_` into `original_args_` in
`GetMutableArgs()` and `CHECK`s in `GetOriginalArgs()` that
`GetMutableArgs()` has not been called, guarded behind
`kAvoidCloneMutableExtensionFunctionArgs` (disabled by default). This is
safe because the only two callers of `GetOriginalArgs()` [6] (in
`ExtensionFunctionDispatcher::DispatchWithCallbackInternal()`) run
synchronously before `RunWithValidation()` [7], where `GetMutableArgs()`
is called.

[1] `GetMutableArgs()` callers (including `SettingsFunction`):
https://source.chromium.org/search?q=GetMutableArgs%20-f:test&ss=chromium%2Fchromium%2Fsrc
[2] Windows Stable pprof:
http://pprof/?id=17bf9272d6aa1108f21f789a338a5974&pivot=%28%5E%7C%5B%5Ea-zA-Z0-9_%3A%5D%29ExtensionFunction%3A%3A%28~ExtensionFunction%7CGetMutableArgs%29&filter=focus%3Aextensions%253A%253AStorageFrontend%253A%253AOnWriteFinished%7C%2528%255E%7C%255B%255Ea-zA-Z0-9_%253A%255D%2529ExtensionFunction%253A%253AGetMutableArgs,focus%3Abase%253A%253AValue%253A%253A~Value%7C%2528%255E%7C%255B%255Ea-zA-Z0-9_%253A%255D%2529ExtensionFunction%253A%253AGetMutableArgs
[3] macOS Stable pprof:
http://pprof/?id=9525667b45c50cc49ee09656e50ae5ed&pivot=%28%5E%7C%5B%5Ea-zA-Z0-9_%3A%5D%29ExtensionFunction%3A%3A%28~ExtensionFunction%7CGetMutableArgs%29&filter=focus%3Aextensions%253A%253AStorageFrontend%253A%253AOnWriteFinished%7C%2528%255E%7C%255B%255Ea-zA-Z0-9_%253A%255D%2529ExtensionFunction%253A%253AGetMutableArgs,focus%3Abase%253A%253AValue%253A%253A~Value%7C%2528%255E%7C%255B%255Ea-zA-Z0-9_%253A%255D%2529ExtensionFunction%253A%253AGetMutableArgs
[4] `std::move(callback).Run(status)` destroys `callback`, releasing the
last `scoped_refptr<ExtensionFunction>` (bound via `this` in [5]) and
running `~ExtensionFunction()` (destroying `args_` / `original_args_`):
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:extensions/browser/api/storage/storage_frontend.cc;l=323;drc=03d8dc3d9e4c3c882e5f05ae1124fb0027348def
[5] `StorageStorageAreaSetFunction::Run` moving `args_` and
binding `this`:
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:extensions/browser/api/storage/storage_api.cc;l=373-384;drc=03d8dc3d9e4c3c882e5f05ae1124fb0027348def
[6] All `GetOriginalArgs()` callers in Chromium:
https://source.chromium.org/search?q=GetOriginalArgs%20-f:test&ss=chromium%2Fchromium%2Fsrc
[7] `GetOriginalArgs()` calls before `RunWithValidation()` in dispatch:
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:extensions/browser/extension_function_dispatcher.cc;l=385-454;drc=03d8dc3d9e4c3c882e5f05ae1124fb0027348def

[fuchsia] Set default headless screen size to 800x600 in test runner

When running tests under Ozone headless without an explicit screen
size override, ui::HeadlessScreen defaults to a 1x1 screen size.
This differs from content_shell's standard 800x600 window size and
Linux headless mode which defaults to 800x600. The 1x1 default causes
select popups in WebPagePopupImpl to clamp to 1 DIP height and causes
fullscreen or maximized windows to collapse to 1x1, leading to
hit-testing failures such as
SitePerProcessHitTestTrustedUserActivationTriggersTest.PopupRenderWidget.

Passing --ozone-override-screen-size=800,600 when
--ozone-platform=headless is active aligns Fuchsia tests with Linux
headless behavior unless a custom screen size or screen info is
already specified by the caller.

[Settings] Add SettingsSection and CreateSettingsSections

Add SettingsSection, the base class for one settings page whose
subclasses register the page's searchable items in their constructors
and update them as runtime state changes.

Add CreateSettingsSections(), which creates the sections for a
SettingsUI. SettingsUI calls it after creating the registry when
kSettingsSearch2026 is enabled and owns the returned sections. It
returns no sections yet, so there is no behavior change until a
follow-up CL (crrev.com/c/8664721) adds AppearanceSection.

[FedCM] Close the dialog in a separate task for the close button

The close and cancel buttons of the FedCM dialog can be pressed while a
dialog view is still running.
FedCmAccountSelectionView::OnCloseButtonClicked() then destroyed the
dialog widget, and the views that were still running, synchronously.
Keep the input check and the metrics in OnCloseButtonClicked(), but post
closing the dialog to a separate task, which does nothing if the dialog
was closed or replaced in the meantime.

parent
8e09e6cee4ab766c7cae7bce97da015f8d19cbb4 [ diff ] 
[cc] Check painted state after worklet idle

When `ClientLayerTreeHostImpl::OnPaintWorkletResultsReady` transitions
the scheduler paint worklet state to idle while invisible,
`ProcessScheduledActions` can force-activate the completed pending tree
and immediately commit a queued main frame in the same loop. If that
new pending tree has dirty paint worklet inputs, it resets
`pending_tree_fully_painted_` to false and dispatches a new asynchronous
paint worklet job.

Check `pending_tree_fully_painted_` alongside `pending_tree_` after
notifying the scheduler so `NotifyPendingTreeFullyPainted` only runs if
the current pending tree is already fully painted. This prevents a
renderer compositor crash (`DCHECK(pending_tree_fully_painted_)`) in the
browser and tests when a tab or WebUI with active paint worklet
animations becomes hidden while a pipelined commit is ready.

Reject StubTabModel in ChromeTabCreator tab creation entry points

Return null from ChromeTabCreator.createNewTab(),
createTabWithWebContents(), and createFrozenTab() when mTabModel is a
StubTabModel.

Otherwise TabBuilder constructs a detached TabImpl before
StubTabModel.addTab() rejects it, throwing UnsupportedOperationException
or leaking the native WebContents when callers such as
TabModelJniBridge.createTab() release C++ ownership upon receiving a
non-null Tab.

Fix flaky modifier-click tests in WindowOpenSplitTabBrowserTest

The 4 tests that use ClickToOpenWindow() (NewTabModifierClick,
NewForegroundTabModifierClick, NewWindowModifierClickWithPopup and
SplitViewModifierClick) flake on Wayland: the simulated click is
sometimes dropped by the renderer, so no window opens, the
WebContentsAddedObserver times out, and WaitForLoadStop(nullptr) then
crashes the test. WidgetInputHandlerManager suppresses input while the
renderer defers commits or main frame updates, and
SimulateEndOfPaintHoldingOnPrimaryMainFrame() only stops the
browser-side paint holding timer.

Append --allow-pre-commit-input in the fixture, as many other browser
tests that simulate input already do.

Raising the test timeouts does not help: the click is lost, not slow.
Probes (--gtest_repeat=20, no retries, 4 tests = 80 runs per row):

linux-arm64-wayland-rel-fyi (UTR, chromium:try):
  baseline                                       24/80 crashed
  --ui-test-action-max-timeout=60000
    --test-launcher-timeout=90000                21/80 crashed
  this change (80 + 160 runs)                     0/240 click losses
x64 mutter (local, testing/xvfb.py --use-mutter):
  baseline                                        5/80 crashed
  raised timeouts                                 5/80 crashed
  this change, all WindowOpenSplitTab* tests      0/500 failed

[🌷] Deflake CustomTabActivityTest#testParallelRequest: await request

CustomTabActivityTest#testParallelRequest previously navigated the
main frame to /echoheader?Cookie while launching a detached parallel
request to /set-cookie?acookie, racing the outgoing main-frame Cookie
request header against the parallel cookie-setting response. Navigate
to mTestPage, wait for CustomTabs.DetachedResourceRequest.FinalStatus
to record NetError.OK via HistogramWatcher, and verify the cookie via
document.cookie to eliminate the race and re-enable the test.

[ozone/wayland] Scale decoration insets by ui_scale in window geometry

When ui_scale != 1, eg: GNOME's "Large Text" accessibility setting
(text-scaling-factor 1.25), toplevel windows treated client-side
decoration insets as Wayland DIP, but CalculateInsetsInDIP() returns
them in UI (ie: ui-scale'd) DIP. WaylandWindow added them to the
configured geometry size before downscaling it by ui_scale, removed them
from the bounds size after upscaling it, and WaylandToplevelWindow used
them unscaled as the window geometry offset.

As a result, the window geometry sent to the compositor did not line up
with the frame drawn by views: with the 10 DIP resize border and Large
Text, it was off by 2.5 DIP per edge, so tiled windows show visible gaps
between each other and the screen edges.

Treat the insets as UI DIP in WaylandWindow's geometry/bounds size
conversions, consistently with WaylandPopup, and offset the window
geometry by round(insets * ui_scale), via a new
WaylandWindow::GetWindowGeometryOriginInWaylandDIP() helper. Since the
surface size in Wayland DIP can no longer be derived exactly from the
geometry size plus insets, compute it from the bounds when there are
insets, like WaylandPopup does.

There is no behavior change when ui_scale is 1.

Bug: 581917233
Test: ozone_unittests --gtest_filter=*UiScale*
Test: Manual: On GNOME Wayland with Large Text enabled, tile two
      windows side by side, verify there are no gaps between them or
      the screen edges.

  base::flat_set<SBThreatType> to base::EnumSet<SBThreatType>, replacing
  heap-allocated vectors with a 4-byte inline bitset.

  HasAll() subset check and update CheckBrowseUrl callers and GetHash
  protocol managers to use EnumSet operations.

  SBThreatTypeSet to deduplicate threat types inline without temporary
  set allocations.

com.google.protobuf.SchemaUtil in protobuf-javalite no longer has
getUnknownFieldSetSchemaClass(), and no longer initializes a
GENERATED_MESSAGE_CLASS static field in <clinit>, leaving
getGeneratedMessageClass() as an uncalled private helper that R8
strips automatically during tree shaking.

before and after removing the rule: classes*.dex and the APK are
bit-for-bit identical.

[Glic][Metrics] Add native FRE metrics and post-accept latency

Update Glic instance metrics for the bottom-sheet native FRE flow:
1. Record the opt-in impression, panel presentation time, and actionable
   time immediately when the native FRE card is shown on open, and
   suppress duplicate impressions from the background web client across
   opens and tab switches.
2. Clear the loading invocation state on native FRE open so pre-accept
   closes count only as FRE declines rather than loading dismissals.
3. Record Glic.Fre.AcceptToChatActionable once the user accepts the FRE
   and the chat UI submits its actionable frame.

[Rust CPSP] Add Android to fieldtrial testing config

This will unblock rolling out the global state CPSP trial to Android.

CL:8376862 added the desktop platforms to the fieldtrial testing config
for `ChildProcessSecurityPolicyRust`, but not Android. This is because
android_browsertests were crashing due to CPSP being initialized before
the FeatureList was available to check if we were in Rust or C++ mode.
This had already been fixed for non-test paths, but the Android
browsertests paths goes through `startup::ValidateLaunchUrlWebUnsafe()`
and `ChildProcessSecurityPolicy::GetInstance()`, which checks the
feature list. Since that earlier attempt, CL:8687436 added an early
return to `ValidateLaunchUrlWebUnsafe()` that would return before the
CPSP call for all URLs that are used in browser tests. Because of that,
we can now add Android to the fieldtrial testing config.

Handle null OTR Profile in ToolbarManager.refreshSelectedTab()

Allow LocationBarModel.setTab() to accept a null Profile when tab is
null so ToolbarManager.refreshSelectedTab() can run its full
tab-clearing and button-updating path when an off-the-record TabModel
has no tabs.

When an Incognito-only window closes its last tab, IncognitoTabModelImpl
destroys its delegate TabModel (making getProfile() return null) while
remaining the selected TabModel because the window's regular TabModel is
a StubTabModel.

[🌷] Deflake DualControlLayoutTest#testInflation: round expected px

DualControlLayout#parseAttributes resolves app:stackedMargin="24dp"
using TypedArray#getDimensionPixelSize, which rounds the scaled pixel
dimension to the nearest integer. Update testInflation to round the
expected 24 * dpToPx value via Math.round() so fractional display
densities on Automotive emulators match the parsed integer margin, and
re-enable the test on Automotive.

[🌷] Re-enable AccountPickerBottomSheetTest#testProfileDataUpdate*

Both testProfileDataUpdateOnExpandedSheet and
testProfileDataUpdateOnInitialExpandedSheet previously failed with
AmbiguousViewMatcherException because updating an already-added account
triggered a full ProfileDataCache rebuild and onAccountsUpdated()
callback, causing AccountPickerMediator to clear and re-populate the
RecyclerView model while DefaultItemAnimator animated the old and new
ViewHolders simultaneously.

Since crrev.com/c/8495709 reduced ProfileDataCache updates with
IdentityManager so known accounts only fire onProfileDataUpdated(), the
existing row PropertyModel is updated in-place without recreating
ViewHolders. Additionally, use AccountManagerTestRule#updateAccount
instead of #addAccount when updating TestAccounts.ACCOUNT1 (which is
already added in setUp()).

[SuperSize] Add experimental .size v2 binary format

Introduce an experimental v2 .size binary format with parallel Zstandard
compression and decompression, while keeping v1.1 as the default output
format behind --format-v2:
- Configure tools/binary_size/libsupersize/vpython.toml for Python 3.14
  to use stdlib compression.zstd.
- Implement v2 binary serialization and deserialization in
  file_format_v2.py and viewer/caspian/file_format_v2.{h,cc}, using
  byte-stream-split 32-bit numeric columns, deduplicated path tuples,
  and sharded front-coded symbol name tables.
- Add --format-v2 (use_v2=False default) to archive, save_diff, and
  console SaveSizeInfo/SaveDeltaSizeInfo.
- Parallelize Caspian v2 blob decompression and name decoding across
  threads.
- Add unit tests in file_format_test.py and file_format_test.cc covering
  v1 and v2 round-trips, and document v2 in docs/file_format.md.

[JS Optimizer] Add kBlockV8OptimizerOnUnfamiliarSites kill switch

Add kBlockV8OptimizerOnUnfamiliarSites (enabled by default) to gate the
option to block JavaScript optimization on unfamiliar sites. This option
is currently available as the middle option on the
chrome://settings/content/v8 page. We are adding this gate so that we
can deprecate the feature and remove it in a future milestone.

Disabling the feature hides the option and disables the associated
functionality. Users who had selected it fall back to "Sites can use
JavaScript optimization". Chrome keeps their stored choice until we
remove the feature in a future milestone.

Disabling the feature also disables the JavaScript optimizations omnibox
icon for all users, including users who block JavaScript optimization
for all sites, specific sites, or through enterprise policy. The icon
and associated bubble are also planned to be removed as a part of this
deprecation.

This changelist partially restores functionality that

Reland "[Keyboard Shortcut Hints] Do not show keyboard shortcut hints on phones"

This is a reland of commit 0d57b3f0ed3ce90b186f5a1d55596cd8a38003e9

The original CL was reverted because
showMenu_verifyShortcutTextPopulatedWhenEnabled in
TabStripContextMenuCoordinatorUnitTest failed on unbranded CI bots
(expected 6 menu items, got 8). Under @Config(qualifiers = "sw600dp"),
sAndroidVerticalTabs defaults to false on branded CQ builds
(defaultValue = false) and true on unbranded CI builds
(defaultValueInTests = true), inserting 2 Vertical Tabs items.
Explicitly disable ANDROID_VERTICAL_TABS on that test method so menu
item assertions are deterministic across branded and unbranded builds.

Original change's description:
> [Keyboard Shortcut Hints] Do not show keyboard shortcut hints on phones
>
> Previously, KeyboardShortcuts.getShortcutText() only checked whether
> kAndroidKeyboardShortcutHints was enabled and whether an alphabetic
> keyboard was attached, so a phone with a connected physical keyboard
> would still display shortcut hints in menus.
>
> Pass the menu window's Context into KeyboardShortcuts.getShortcutText()
> and check DeviceFormFactor.isNonMultiDisplayContextOnTablet(context) in
> shouldShowShortcutHints() so shortcut hints are only shown on tablet and
> desktop displays (including split-screen windows on tablets and external
> desktop monitors).
>

Deliver ReportingObserver reports without a report-to endpoint

COOP access reports and Connection-Allowlist violation reports were
only queued when the document declared a report-to endpoint, so a
ReportingObserver on a page without one never got them. The endpoint
controls network upload, not observer delivery.

Queue reports for observers independently of the endpoint, and keep
network upload endpoint-gated. For COOP, only documents with a
COOP-Report-Only policy monitor accesses. An opener with enforced COOP
but no report-only policy no longer receives reports for the popup's
policy.

Add WPTs covering both report types without report-to and an enforced
COOP opener accessing a COOP-Report-Only popup.

Migrate LanguagePrefs to base::i18n::LanguageTag

LanguagePrefs exposes the accept and user-selected languages as lists
of strings, which callers like TranslatePrefs parse into LanguageTags,
and convert back to strings to update them.

Make LanguagePrefs take and return LanguageTags instead, using the
language_tag_list_helper.h helpers to parse and serialize the prefs:
- GetAcceptLanguagesList(), GetUserSelectedLanguagesList() and the
  Android-only GetULPLanguages() return vectors of LanguageTags.
- SetUserSelectedLanguagesList() takes a span of LanguageTags.
- IsForcedLanguage() takes a LanguageTag.
- l10n_util::KeepAcceptedLanguages(), which is only used by
  LanguagePrefs, takes and returns LanguageTags.

This removes the string round trips from TranslatePrefs.

Since the accept languages pref is now built from parsed language tags,
malformed tags are dropped from it and the other ones are canonicalized
(e.g. "en_us" -> "en-US"), which also applies when deduplicating the
policy-forced languages.

GetFirstLanguage(), GetLanguagesWithMaxCount() and
GetIncognitoLanguageList(), which compute the Accept-Language header
from the raw pref value, are unchanged.

[TabGroup] Deflake TabGroupListRenderTest#testGroupPane

In TabGroupListRenderTest, creating new tab groups programmatically
triggers TabGroupListMediator#repopulateModelList(), which clears and
re-adds all rows to the ModelList. By default, RecyclerView's
DefaultItemAnimator sets alpha to 0 on newly added row view holders and
delays starting the add fade-in animation by removeDuration (120ms).

Because Espresso's waitForView(withText(title)) checks isDisplayed()
(which only checks visibility and layout bounds but ignores view
alpha), waitForView succeeded while the newly added rows were still
at alpha = 0. The subsequent render(recyclerView, ...) captured a
blank image (rgba(0,0,0,0)). The previous workaround used a hardcoded
Thread.sleep(300), which was prone to flakes under bot load if
animations were delayed.

Fix this by setting the RecyclerView's itemAnimator to null and waiting
for the RecyclerView to stabilize with waitForStableRecyclerView().
This completely eliminates view alpha zeroing and avoids arbitrary
sleeps.

[glic] Confirm user Back/Forward restored from BFCache

while an actor task runs in a tab, user navigations away from the page
show the leave confirmation from ActorNavigationThrottle. A user
Back/Forward that restores a page from BFCache shows no confirmation and
leaves the page at once.

BFCache restores skip NavigationThrottles, so ActorNavigationThrottle
never sees them. ActorCommitDeferringCondition runs for these restores,
but it only applies origin gating and never asks the user.

Fix: Catch the back navigation: When a user clicks Back to restore a
page from BFCache, ActorCommitDeferringCondition intercepts it right
before it commits and pauses it.

Check who pressed Back: Check whether the Back was triggered by the user
or by the Actor itself (HistoryTool). If it was, we let it through
without asking.

Ask the user ("Leave site and end task?"): If the user pressed Back,pop
up the confirmation dialog asking if they really want to leave.

Handle their choice: If they click "Leave": Stop the Actor task cleanly
(kUserNavigatedAway) and resume the page so they go back. If they click
"Stay": Call WebContents::Stop() to cancel the back navigation, so the
user stays on the page and the Actor task keeps working.

Track static ES module imports in ScriptAncestryTracker

Static module imports (`import { x } from './sub.js'`) previously
bypassed `ScriptAncestryTracker`, `AdTracker`, and
`ExtensionScriptTracker` because:
1. `JSModuleScript::Create` compiles modules via `ModuleRecord::Compile`
   and `ModuleTreeLinker` only instantiates/evaluates the root module,
   so V8 links and evaluates submodules internally without invoking
   `probe::ExecuteScript` for them.
2. `ModuleTreeLinker::FetchDescendants` discovers child imports
   asynchronously when neither the parent module nor the creating
   script's `AsyncTaskContext` is on the stack.

This CL:
- Adds `ModuleScript::AsyncTaskContext()` and registers compiled module
  scripts in `JSModuleScript::Create` via
  `ScriptInitiationMonitor::DidCompileModuleScript`, passing explicit
  `is_inline` source location info to `RegisterScriptWithUrl` and
  associating marked modules with their `AsyncTaskContext`.
- Enters a `probe::AsyncTask` using `module_script->AsyncTaskContext()`
  in `ModuleTreeLinker::FetchDescendants` when initiating descendant
  fetches.
- Adds `probe::AsyncTaskContext` to `ModuleScriptLoader` so initiating
  script and parent module provenance is preserved across asynchronous
  module fetches to `JSModuleScript::Create`.
- Adds `SimTest` coverage for linear, branching, inline,
  evaluation-time, circular, and diamond static module import graphs,
  including negative (unmarked) tests and fragment URL inline module
  registration.

Remove CanUseFragmentsFor{Ink,Visual}Overflow().

Remove CanUseFragmentsForVisualOverflow() from LayoutBox, and
CanUseFragmentsForInkOverflow() from PhysicalBoxFragment.

This is achieved by removing LayoutReplaced::RecalcVisualOverflow(), and
then hoist LayoutBlock::RecalcVisualOverflow() to LayoutBox, and have
PhysicalBoxFragment defer to
LayoutReplaced::ComputeContentsVisualOverflow() for replaced content
fragments, instead of doing its own normal thing.

No behavior changes intended.

[🌷] Deflake WebApkUpdateIntegrationTest#testStoreUpdateRequestToFile

WebApkUpdateIntegrationTest#testStoreUpdateRequestToFile previously
loaded manifest.json (which lists 6 icons of various sizes) while
populating the test WebAPK metadata with only 512x512 icon URLs. On
160dpi displays such as android-14-automotive-landscape-x64-rel,
ManifestIconSelector picks the 192x192 icon as the splash icon
instead of image-512px.png, resulting in 4 icons in the update
request proto instead of 3. Use manifest_one_icon.json via
WebappTestPage.getTestUrlWithManifest so image-512px.png is selected
consistently across all display densities, and re-enable the test on
Automotive.

[Isolated Mode] Skip off-store file data collection in Isolated Mode

Enterprise Isolated Mode profiles share their extensions with the parent
profile, whose ExtensionTelemetryService already hashes the files of
off-store extensions. Repeating that work for the Isolated Mode instance
would only duplicate disk I/O.

SetUpOffstoreFileDataCollection() now returns early for Isolated Mode
profiles. Their reports still include file data, read from the parent's
kExtensionTelemetryFileData pref.

[WebApp] Reject non-standard and pseudo-MIME types in file_handlers

Previously, net::IsValidTopLevelMimeType accepted any top-level MIME
type starting with "x-" (except "x-scheme-handler"), and OS file
handling integration only filtered out "x-scheme-handler/*". On
FreeDesktop/Linux desktops, other "x-*" top-level pseudo-MIME types
such as "x-content/*" (removable media autorun), "x-directory/*", and
"x-special/*" are used for non-file OS associations, and custom "x-*"
top-level types are not valid IANA top-level media types for web app
file handlers. Furthermore, Manifest::ValidateInvariants,
FileHandlingSubManager, and ParseWebAppProto did not previously reject
all "x-*" top-level MIME types.

This change:
1. Updates net::IsValidTopLevelMimeType to reject FreeDesktop
   pseudo-MIME top-level types ("x-scheme-handler", "x-content",
   "x-directory", and "x-special").
2. Adds blink::IsValidFileHandlerMimeType in
   third_party/blink/public/common/manifest/manifest_util.h to validate
   that a file handler MIME type parses as a parameterless type/subtype
   with a standard IANA top-level media type (excluding "x-*" top-level
   types).
3. Uses blink::IsValidFileHandlerMimeType across ManifestParser,
   Manifest::ValidateInvariants, PopulateFileHandlerInfoFromManifest,
   ParseWebAppProto, FileHandlingSubManager, and Linux .desktop / MIME
   registration generators.
4. Updates ShortcutSubManager::Execute to also recreate shortcuts on
   Linux (in addition to macOS) when file_handling state changes, since
   Linux .desktop files embed file handling MimeType metadata.

[omnibox][webUI] Fix bugs with tabbing to keyword chip with query

**Background**

Users can tab into keyword mode with a query; e.g., they type 'bing.com
<backspace>query<tab>'. Or without a query; e.g., they type 'bin<tab>'.

When doing so without a query: a) popup selection is traversed & b)
omnibox enters keyword mode, but c) autocomplete is not re-run and d)
the popup results are not changed. This allows the user to continue
tabbing past the chip or shift+tabbing back from it.

When doing so with a query the behavior is views/full-webUI dependent.

**Bug 1 - tab traversal in views**

In views and webUI popup, tabbing into a keyword chip with a query would
c) re-run autocomplete and d) the popup results would change. This would
prevent users from tabbing past the chip or shift+tabbing back from it.

**Bug 2 - enter navigation in full webUI**

In full webUI, tabbing into a keyword chip with a query would behave
like without a query; i.e. c) not re-run autocomplete and not interfere
with further tab traversal. But e) pressing enter would do nothing,
preventing the user from navigating to the default keyword-with-query
search match.

                      | Tab traversal   | Enter navigation
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Views       w/o query | no clobber      | does nothing (correct)
WebUI popup w/o query | no clobber      | does nothing (correct)
Full webUI  w/o query | no clobber      | does nothing (correct)
Views       w/  query | results clobber | navigates    (correct)
WebUI popup w/  query | results clobber | navigates    (correct)
Full webUI  w/  query | no clobber      | does nothing (incorrect)

**New behavior**

This CL fixes both bugs and consolidates behavior across all 4 cases:
(with and without query) x (views, webUI popup, full webUI).

With this CL, all cases will c) not re-run autocompletion, d) not change
popup results, allowing further tabbing, and e) enter will navigate even
when a keyword chip is focused as long as there is a query. This
requires running an extra Autocomplete classification pass, since
keyword chips don't have a navigation URL.

                      | Tab traversal   | Enter navigation
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Views       w/o query | no clobber      | does nothing
WebUI popup w/o query | no clobber      | does nothing
Full webUI  w/o query | no clobber      | does nothing
Views       w/  query | no clobber      | navigates
WebUI popup w/  query | no clobber      | navigates
Full webUI  w/  query | no clobber      | navigates

[🌷] Deflake NewTabPageTest#testClickPlusButtonOnFakebox: skip on Auto

NewTabPageTest#testClickPlusButtonOnFakebox failed on Automotive
builders because Fusebox and the NTP fakebox plus button are
intentionally unsupported on Automotive devices
(OmniboxCapabilities#isFuseboxSupportedDeviceType returns
!DeviceInfo.isAutomotive()), leaving R.id.search_box_plus_button as
View.GONE with 0x0 dimensions. Additionally, while the test was
disabled, the NTP plus button visibility and focus behavior were
gated behind OmniboxMultimodalInput parameters
show_ntp_plus_button/true and
focus_fusebox_from_ntp_plus_button/true. Restrict the test to
non-automotive devices via
@Restriction(DeviceRestriction.RESTRICTION_TYPE_NON_AUTO), enable
both parameters, and re-enable the test.

[COS] Copy staging write chunks before writing to disk and hashing

Previously, CrossOriginStorageStagingWriter read the input buffer twice:
once to write it to disk, and a second time to compute its hash. When
reading from a Mojo data pipe, the renderer could change the buffer
between those two reads, causing the hash not to match the file on disk.

This CL fixes this by copying each 64 KiB chunk into a local buffer
first, then using that copy for both the disk write and the hash.

TAG=agy

40f41377f6127741b125b656e7565c6f22a479e3 [ diff ] 
Restore Partial Translate context menu item on PDFs

https://crrev.com/c/8344374 (crbug.com/555282656) allowed PDF pages to
be registered for language detection when kEnableTranslatePdf is
disabled so that Partial Translate ("Translate selection to [language]")
could determine the source language. Because IsMimeTypeSupported()
returned true for application/pdf unconditionally, that inadvertently
enabled Full Page Translation on PDFs and caused a crash when reverting
translation on a PluginDocument (crbug.com/565171599).

https://crrev.com/c/8516938 fixed that crash by making
TranslateManager::IsMimeTypeSupported() return false for application/pdf
when kEnableTranslatePdf is disabled. However, RenderViewContextMenu
gates Partial Translate behind CanTranslate(/*menu_logging=*/false),
which delegates to TranslateManager::CanManuallyTranslate(). Because
CanManuallyTranslate() checks IsMimeTypeSupported(), it returned false
on PDFs and hid the "Translate selection to [language]" context menu
item when kEnableTranslatePdf is disabled.

This CL introduces TranslateManager::CanPartiallyTranslate() (which
allows application/pdf regardless of kEnableTranslatePdf) and updates
RenderViewContextMenu to check CanPartiallyTranslate() for
AppendPartialTranslateItem() while keeping full-page translation gated
on CanTranslate() and disabled for PDFs when kEnableTranslatePdf is
disabled.
